newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil futures bourse to launch FRB bond contract.
newsitem.headline: Brazil futures bourse to launch FRB bond contract.

text.p: The Brazilian futures exchange Bolsa de Mercadorias & Futuros (BM&F) said it plans to launch futures on Argentina's Floating Rate Bond (FRB) on December 6, the exchange said in a statement.
The bourse said it had initially set the launching for Thursday, November 28, but postponed it because trade is expected to be thin that day due to the Thanksgiving Day holiday in the United States.
The U.S. dollar-denominated contracts will have a face value of $50,000 and the trading price will be based on a discount or premium of up to 100 basis points.
The FRB contracts are most likely to be traded by banks that trade Brady bonds in the spot market, a BM&F spokeswoman said.
FRB bonds were issued by Argentina on March 31, 1993, as a part of a foreign debt rescheduling scheme with international creditors. The bonds mature March 31, 2005.
BM&F has an average daily turnover of $14 billion, with some 500,000 contracts, making it the world's fourth largest futures exchange.
